author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. Sen. Jack Reed won Rhode Island’s Democratic Senate primary, according to results published by the Rhode Island Board of Elections after Wednesday’s voting.

Reed faced challenger Connor Burbridge for the nomination. The state results page showed Reed advancing, while election officials continued the routine canvass and certification process. Published election-night totals are unofficial until that work is complete, including review of eligible mail ballots and any provisional ballots.

The outcome places Reed on the November ballot alongside Republican nominee Raymond McKay and independent candidate Michael Bahry. The general election will determine who represents Rhode Island in the six-year Senate term beginning in January. This article reports the primary result and does not assess or predict the general-election contest.

The Senate race was one of several statewide and municipal contests on Rhode Island’s primary ballot. With nominations now largely settled, candidates move into a shorter fall campaign in which federal policy, household costs and local priorities are expected to remain prominent. Voters can use the Board of Elections results portal for updated totals and official certification information.
dek: Official state results showed the incumbent advancing from Wednesday’s primary, setting the U.S. Senate field for the November general election.
headline: Jack Reed wins Rhode Island Democratic U.S. Senate primary
